clue.text: Sad record playing, accordingly slow

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a record that is playing is on
so means therefore, accordingly
a clock that is slow shows a time that is late

explanation.surface: A melancholy song is played at a mournfully slow tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sad record played slowly, but every word after the first is a separate short piece; 'slow' works the way a clock runs slow or late.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disconsolate is unhappy beyond comforting, a stronger synonym for sad.

clue.text: Look cursorily, look over degree certificate

parts.note: to dip into a book is to look at it cursorily
lo is an old exclamation meaning look
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Someone glances quickly at a graduate's degree certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' just keeps the clue's order, one piece above the next, so it joins rather than rearranges. The old exclamation for look is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is the document awarded on completing a course of study, a kind of certificate.

clue.text: Row around river to find fish

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it on both sides

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel, a row
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone rows round a river hunting for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a verb for rowing a boat, but it is the noun meaning a quarrel (rhymes with cow).
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery herring-like sea fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Speech holding up record for campaign

indicators.note: to hold is to grip something inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A political address that delays the release of a record during an election campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' looks like one phrase meaning delaying, but it splits: 'holding' encloses, and 'up' turns the record over.
explanation.definitionFit: A military campaign is an organised operation, a set of planned actions toward an objective.

clue.text: Queen with waves, on brand

indicators.note: in a down entry, something placed on another sits above it, so the later piece goes first

parts.note: the waves stand for the sea
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch waving to the crowd while staying on message for her brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' suggests a royal wave of the hand, but it means the sea. 'On' puts the sea above the queen's single letter in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand cattle is to burn a mark into the hide, which is to sear it with hot iron.

clue.text: Underwear that is put underneath last

indicators.note: placing one thing underneath another in a down light means it comes lower, so it is written second

parts.note: to last is to linger, to stay on
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Advice that underwear goes on underneath, before anything else is put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like 'final' but is the verb meaning endure; 'put underneath' sends IE below it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightclothes, typically delicate garments.

clue.text: Temperature suitable, say, for stock

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: 'say' asks for how a word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: suitable means right, which is pronounced the same as a ceremonial rite

explanation.surface: A cook judging the right temperature for making stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests soup in a kitchen, but here it is the adjective, as in a stock phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock response is a standard, overused one, and trite means hackneyed and unoriginal.

clue.text: Unpredictable changes of silver in metamorphoses

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: read as a verb, metamorphoses means changes, varies
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver's appearance shifts unpredictably as it goes through transformations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metamorphoses' looks like a plural noun but is the verb, he metamorphoses, so it means 'varies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagaries are erratic, whimsical departures from the expected course, as in the vagaries of the weather.

clue.text: Infinite divinity restrains Church hypocrisy

indicators.note: something infinite has no end, so the word loses its final letter
to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a deity is a divinity; without its end it loses the Y
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An eternal god keeps the Church from being hypocritical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infinite divinity' reads naturally as an all-powerful god; cryptically it is a god without an end, DEIT(Y).
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocrisy is pretending to virtues you lack, a form of deceit or dishonest pretence.

clue.text: China got richer, occasionally in open

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: open means plain, clear for all to see

indicators.note: doing something occasionally means only now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters: gOt RiChEr

explanation.surface: China grew wealthier, at times in full public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' poses as the country getting richer, but it is the definition: fine crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for porcelain, the fine ceramic first made in that country.

clue.text: Initially irked, rather annoyed, then enraged

definitions.text: Initially irked, rather annoyed, then enraged

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: Someone's mood escalates from mild irritation through annoyance to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: its five words' first letters spell IRATE, and the clue describes someone getting angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising from irked to enraged describes growing anger, and irate means very angry.

clue.text: Old bag of bones

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
to bag something is to take it, steal it

explanation.surface: An old sack full of bones, or a scrawny old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bag' reads as a rude phrase for an old woman; 'bag' is the verb, as in bagging a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is the technical adjective for anything relating to bone, from the Greek osteon.

clue.text: Influence of rejected party facing decline

indicators.note: to face something is to stand in front of it, so this piece comes first
something rejected is sent back, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A political party voted out loses influence as it goes into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, matching 'rejected' and 'decline', but it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is power to sway decisions, the advantage that lets someone exert influence.

clue.text: Female consumed by a fine romance

indicators.note: what is consumed is taken inside, so one piece is swallowed by the other

parts.note: 'a' as written, and fine means fair, as fair weather
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman swept up in a fine romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Fine Romance' is a famous song title, which makes the last words feel like one phrase; 'fine' gives FAIR, with F slipped in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a love relationship, often secret or short-lived, so a romance.

clue.text: Notorious criminal executed in abandoned fort

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
an abandoned building is empty, so the word is emptied of its middle and keeps its outside

parts.note: the outside letters of fort
an old lag is a habitual criminal, British slang for a convict
to execute a plan is to run it

explanation.surface: A notorious outlaw is put to death inside a deserted fort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' wants to mean put to death; here it means carried out, ran.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and conspicuous, notorious in the sense of shockingly obvious.

clue.text: Cop leading tough precinct

indicators.note: something leading goes in front, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
tough means strict, harsh in discipline

explanation.surface: A police officer in charge of a rough patch of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough precinct' reads as a dangerous neighbourhood, but 'tough' describes the cop's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is a defined area of a town, such as a police or administrative district.

clue.text: Sign is outside the man's storehouse

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it on both sides

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
the man's is he's, contracted

explanation.surface: A notice hangs outside a man's warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' suggests a shop sign; it is the star sign. 'The man's' is read as 'the man is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word means treasure-house, and a thesaurus is a storehouse of words.

clue.text: Flounder's easily keeping submerged

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the letters are held inside the words

parts.note: eight letters run consecutively across these words, starting after the F and ending before the S of the second

explanation.surface: A flatfish has no trouble staying underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' suggests the flatfish, which fits the watery surface, or a verb meaning struggle; it only supplies letters: fl-UNDER'S EA-sily.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersea means situated or happening below the surface of the sea, as something submerged is.

clue.text: Still name insect after beetle family

indicators.note: what comes after follows, so these pieces are written second

parts.note: the stag is a family of beetles, named for the male's antler-like jaws
N is the standard abbreviation for name
the ant is the crossword's favourite insect

explanation.surface: Someone is still deciding what to call an insect from a beetle family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like the adverb 'yet'; it is the adjective meaning motionless, as in still water.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water is still and not flowing, often stale as a result.

clue.text: Just beginning to seem intimate

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of seem
to intimate is to hint at, imply

explanation.surface: A relationship that is only now starting to feel close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' poses as the adjective meaning close; it is the verb meaning hint, stressed on the last syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and simply are interchangeable adverbs meaning merely, as in 'it's just a game'.

clue.text: Gutted Conservative negates useless count

indicators.note: a gutted thing has its insides removed, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the outside letters of Conservative
the outside letters of negates, gutted too
U/S is the abbreviation for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A devastated Tory dismisses a pointless vote count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' reads as British slang for bitterly disappointed, but it empties both following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population, so a count in its formal sense.

clue.text: Doubt party accepts American poll's leader

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece takes the others inside

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
US is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of poll

explanation.surface: Questions raised as a party embraces the frontrunner in an American election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubt' is a verb here, and SUSPECT works as the verb too: I suspect it.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect something is to be inclined to doubt or mistrust it without proof.

clue.text: Flash vehicle saves energy as well

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash, British informal

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a Rover is a car, from the British carmaker
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A flashy car is also economical with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' reads as an adjective meaning showy, British slang; here it is a noun, an instant. E goes in after the first letter of the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreover and 'as well' both introduce an extra point, meaning besides or in addition.

clue.text: Spurned lover upset about past

indicators.note: in a down entry, something upset is turned upside down, so it reads from the bottom
these words are wrapped about the solution, which lies inside them

parts.note: five letters run consecutively across the join: spur-NED LO-ver

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor is distressed over what has happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurned lover' tempts you to look for a word like EX; the answer is hidden backwards in it, and reading NEDLO upwards gives OLDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden is an old-fashioned adjective for bygone times, as in the olden days, so past.

clue.text: Dish providing full stomach?

parts.note: surface reading: a filling meal that leaves you full
setter's reading: the dish literally is a stomach that has been stuffed full

explanation.walkthrough: The traditional Scottish pudding is minced sheep's offal, oatmeal and spices cooked inside a sheep's stomach, so it is a full stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a dish whose casing is traditionally an animal's stomach packed with seasoned filling.

clue.text: Embrace sweetheart then moan

parts.note: to embrace is to clasp or grip
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Hug your partner, then start complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover but splits as sweet's heart, a common crossword trick for E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is a complaint, and to gripe is to grumble or moan.

clue.text: Work is endless for boss

indicators.note: having no end means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to study is to work at learning; cut short it loses its Y

explanation.surface: Someone working for the boss feels the work never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' wants to be the employer, but it is a raised knob or ornament on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round projecting knob, such as the stud on a shield or a decorative stud.

clue.text: Scored five hundred following boundary

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this piece is written second

parts.note: a line marks a boundary
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A batsman reaches five hundred runs with a boundary, a cricket shot that reaches the edge of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' and 'boundary' build a cricket scene; 'scored' means marked with lines, not making runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper scored with marks is lined, so scored as a past participle means ruled with lines.

clue.text: Stern is stable circling round island

indicators.note: something circling goes all the way around, enclosing what is inside

parts.note: mentally stable means sane
a turn is a round, as in taking your turn
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A ship's rear stays steady as it circles round an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' poses as the back of a boat, beside 'island', but it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a gloomy, grave, forbidding temperament, close to stern in manner.

clue.text: Brilliant ancestry of ancient people?

parts.note: Incan means belonging to the Incas, an ancient people of Peru
descent is ancestry, lineage

explanation.surface: A dazzling family tree traced back to an ancient civilisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: the answer split in two reads as 'Incan descent', the lineage of a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing with heat, hence brilliantly bright, a figurative synonym for dazzling.
